**VidCraft: Intelligent Prompt-Driven Video Generation Pipeline**

# 1\. Project Abstract

VidCraft is an end-to-end AI-powered cinematic video generation pipeline designed to assist users in producing high-quality video content through natural language prompts. The system bridges the gap between creative intent and technically precise video generation by integrating multiple intelligent layers: a local natural language processing engine for prompt analysis, a large language model for prompt enhancement and a dual-mode video generation strategy that dramatically reduces cost.

The core innovation of VidCraft lies in its dual-generation approach. Users who require low cost or free generation can leverage a Remotion-based programmatic video rendering engine, which produces animated videos from code using React and CSS timelines, with no per-generation API fee. Users who require photorealistic output can route their enhanced prompts through a curated selection of AI video generation APIs, prioritizing providers offering free credits or trial tiers before falling back to pay-per-generation options. This hybrid strategy makes high-quality video generation accessible to individuals with minimal budgets.

Additional components include different style themes configurator, FFmpeg based post processing and an optional audio synthesis layer using text to speech services. The React based frontend provides a prompt authoring studio, real time generation progress tracking via Web Socket and a prompt version history timeline. VidCraft is implemented as a four member collaborative FYP, spanning from May 2026 to April 2027 across ten structured development phases.

# 2\. Introduction

The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence has unlocked the ability to produce video content from textual descriptions. However, the quality of AI-generated video is highly sensitive to the precision and richness of the input prompt. Vague or poorly structured prompts yield generic, low quality output, while well-crafted prompts produce visually compelling results. Most users lack the expertise to write such prompts unaided and the cost of iterative API based generation makes experimentation expensive.

VidCraft addresses both problems simultaneously. On the prompt quality side, the system applies a spaCy-based natural language analysis pipeline to score prompts across five dimensions: subject clarity, action specificity, environment detail, visual richness and temporal coherence. A locally hosted large language model then rewrites weak prompts into structured descriptions informed by the user's chosen style parameters. On the cost side, VidCraft introduces a programmatic video generation pathway using Remotion, a React-based video rendering framework, which allows animated educational and narrative videos to be rendered entirely from code at near zero marginal cost.

External video generation APIs are incorporated with a tiered selection strategy: free-trial providers are prioritized and paid providers are accessed only when free quotas are exhausted. A structured React frontend, real-time Socket.IO notifications and FFmpeg post-processing complete the pipeline, delivering a production ready video studio experience.

The project is structured into nine development phases spanning 11 to 12 months, with each of the four team members assigned clear module ownership aligned to their domain expertise. VidCraft targets students, educators, small content creators and researchers who need high quality video generation without the overhead of mastering AI prompt engineering or paying large generation fees.

# 3\. Success Criterion

The project will be considered successful if the following measurable outcomes are achieved by the end of April 2027:

- The LLM-based prompt enhancer demonstrably increases the mean quality score across a test set of 50 raw user prompts, with a statistically measurable average score improvement documented in the final report.
- The Remotion-based programmatic generation pathway successfully renders at least three distinct animated video compositions from a single enhanced text prompt, producing downloadable MP4 files without any external API cost.
- The external API integration layer successfully generates at least one real video through a connected free-tier provider, with the full pipeline completing within an acceptable time window.
- The React frontend, including the style configurator, real-time progress tracker and prompt version timeline, is fully functional and mobile-responsive.
- The complete end-to-end pipeline, from frontend prompt submission to video delivery via WebSocket, completes at least one successful run demonstrated live during the demonstration.

Projects exceeding the criterion will include accurate audio narration generated by a text-to-speech service synchronised to the rendered video.

# 4\. Related Work

Research in AI-powered video generation has progressed rapidly since the introduction of diffusion-based image synthesis. Text-to-video models such as Sora (OpenAI, 2024), Veo (Google DeepMind, 2024) and Kling (Kuaishou, 2024) have demonstrated the feasibility of generating seconds long photorealistic video clips from natural language descriptions. These systems however, assume the user can provide high quality prompts and charge significant per-second generation fees, making iterative development costly.

Prompt engineering for generative models has been studied extensively. Researchers have shown that structured, dimension-specific prompts significantly outperform free-form descriptions in generation quality. Tools such as PromptBase and manual prompt marketplaces have emerged commercially, but no open academic system provides automated, linguistically-grounded prompt analysis and enhancement tailored specifically to video generation.

Programmatic video generation represents an alternative paradigm. Remotion (Jonny Burger, 2021) introduced React-based declarative video production, enabling developers to produce animated videos using familiar web development skills. The Manim library (3Blue1Brown, 2015) similarly pioneered code-driven mathematical animation. These tools have been used widely in educational content creation but have not been integrated with AI prompt enhancement pipelines or API-based video generation in a unified studio system.

Semantic embedding models such as Sentence-BERT and its derivatives have been applied to document retrieval, duplicate detection and semantic search. Their application to prompt version tracking and cinematic similarity matching, as implemented in VidCraft, represents a novel usage not documented in prior literature. Similarly, the use of spaCy dependency parsing for prompt quality scoring in the video domain is an original contribution of this project.

The cost optimization strategy employed by VidCraft, specifically the tiered API selection and programmatic fallback approach has not been proposed in any prior academic work on video generation pipelines. Existing systems either rely solely on expensive generation APIs or on purely programmatic tools. VidCraft is the first student level system to combine both within a single orchestration layer.

# 5\. Project Rationale

Video is the dominant medium for online communication, education and creative expression. The barrier to professional-quality video production however, remains high: traditional production requires specialist software, equipment and expertise while AI generation APIs require both prompt engineering skill and significant financial expenditure. VidCraft is motivated by the need to democratize video generation by solving these two barriers simultaneously through intelligent prompt assistance and a cost stratified generation strategy.

The project is additionally motivated by the practical constraints of an academic development team. By building a dual-generation pipeline, VidCraft ensures that the system remains functional and demonstrable throughout development even when API budgets are exhausted, using programmatic Remotion rendering as a reliable fallback. This design decision has both engineering and pedagogical merit.

## 5.1 Aims and Objectives

The primary aim of VidCraft is to build an end-to-end intelligent video generation pipeline that is accessible to users with no prompt engineering expertise and minimal financial budget. The specific objectives are:

- Develop a system that generates well-crafted images and videos from simple text prompts.
- Improve user prompts to create better and more detailed output.
- Provide both free and low-cost video generation options for users.
- Create a user-friendly interface for image and video creation and progress tracking.
- Build an efficient pipeline for video rendering, editing and delivery.

## 5.2 Scope of the Project

The scope of VidCraft is to design and develop a complete AI-powered image and video generation system that transforms user text prompts into cinematic video output. The project focuses on building an efficient, low-cost and user-friendly pipeline that supports prompt analysis, enhancement, media generation and final delivery.

The project work includes the following goals, features and deliverables:

- Develop a React-based frontend that allows users to enter prompts, select theme styles, track generation progress and view prompt history.
- Build a Node.js and Express backend to manage API communication, job scheduling, data handling and real-time processing.
- Create a Python FastAPI AI service for prompt analysis, prompt enhancement, semantic matching and colour grading operations.
- Implement a Remotion-based rendering engine capable of generating animated MP4 videos directly from code.
- Design an FFmpeg post-processing module for thumbnail creation, subtitle overlay, video optimization and compression.
- Add an optional text-to-speech narration feature for synchronized audio generation.
- Store prompts, videos, styles and project data using MongoDB for better performance.
- Perform system integration, testing, debugging and performance evaluation to ensure smooth end-to-end video generation.
- Complete development, documentation, experimentation and final project demonstration within the planned schedule.

## 5.3 Socio-Economic Benefit of the Project

- VidCraft provides an affordable and accessible platform for AI-based media creation for students, educators, freelancers and small content creators.
- The project reduces the cost of cinematic video generation through a low-cost and free rendering pathway using the Remotion engine.
- It makes AI video creation accessible for schools, universities, training centres and non-profit organizations with limited budgets.
- VidCraft helps students learn prompt writing, AI-based content generation and creative media production through interactive feedback and prompt enhancement.
- The project promotes practical learning and improves digital skills in artificial intelligence and multimedia technologies.
- Small businesses and independent creators can produce professional-quality promotional and educational videos without expensive software or production teams.
- The system supports online businesses, digital marketing, freelancing and educational content creation.
- Users can choose between free and premium video generation options according to their financial capacity.
- The project makes advanced AI video technology available to a wider community at minimal cost.

# 6\. Proposed Methodology and Architecture

VidCraft adopts a layered microservice architecture separating the React frontend, the Node.js backend and the Python AI microservice into independently deployable components communicating over HTTP and WebSocket.

## 6.1 Prompt Analysis Layer

Raw user text is submitted to a FastAPI endpoint hosting a spaCy en_core_web_sm analysis pipeline. The pipeline applies dependency parsing to detect subject presence, part-of-speech tagging to confirm action verb coverage, named entity recognition to identify setting and location references and a custom domain-specific antonym dictionary to detect visually contradictory word pairs. The output is a structured JSON object containing an overall 0-100 quality score, a five-dimension breakdown (subject, action, setting, visual, temporal) and natural-language improvement suggestions.

## 6.2 Prompt Enhancement Layer

Prompts scoring below a configurable threshold are passed to the Ollama local inference server running phi3-mini (3.8B parameters), which rewrites the prompt into a rich cinematic description incorporating subject, action, environment, lighting, camera movement, colour tone and mood. Style tokens selected by the user through the Style DNA configurator are injected into the enhancement prompt. A sentence transformer embedding similarity check confirms that the enhanced prompt preserves the original intent. In cases where local inference is unavailable or produces unsatisfactory output quality, the module falls back to a cloud-based language model API, selectable from Claude Sonnet, GPT-4o Mini, Gemini Pro or DeepSeek, chosen based on cost and availability.

## 6.3 Dual-Mode Video Generation

VidCraft implements two complementary video generation strategies:

Programmatic Generation (Remotion): The enhanced prompt is parsed to extract semantic components - subject, action, setting, mood and style tokens. These components are mapped to pre-built Remotion React compositions that use React 19 and Remotion 4 primitives to animate scenes declaratively using CSS timelines. This approach produces animated MP4 videos without any external API call.

API-Based Generation: For photorealistic output, the enhanced prompt is submitted to an external AI video generation API via a Bull.js asynchronous job queue. The system selects the appropriate provider following a tiered priority strategy described in the Tools and Technologies section. The job queue ensures the server never blocks during the 30-120 second generation window; a Socket.IO connection pushes a real-time status update to the connected frontend client upon completion.

## 6.4 Semantic Embedding and Version Tracking

Every submitted prompt, before and after enhancement, is embedded using the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence transformer model, producing a 384-dimensional vector stored in MongoDB. A token-level diff engine using Python difflib compares successive prompt versions and classifies each change into one of four semantic components - subject, action, setting or style - providing structured change attribution for the frontend version timeline.

## 6.5 Post-Processing Pipeline

Generated videos, whether from Remotion or external APIs, pass through a four-step FFmpeg post-processing pipeline: frame extraction for thumbnail generation, OpenCV colour grading applying any filters, optional subtitle caption overlay from enhanced prompt keywords and H.264 compression for web-optimized delivery. Final files are served via Cloudinary on the cloud pathway or directly via Node.js file serving for local Remotion output.

## 6.6 Audio Generation (Optional)

An optional audio narration layer syntheses speech from the enhanced prompt text using a cost stratified text-to-speech selection: Google Cloud Text-to-Speech is the primary option; Azure Cognitive Services TTS serves as an alternative; ElevenLabs is available for higher-quality voice synthesis where budget permits. The generated audio is synchronized to the rendered video using FFmpeg audio stream merging.
